title: The Broken Cask - Welcome to the Mangy Monk - Part 1
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qabDQ1ebZbQ

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens the doors of the Mangy Monk in *The Broken Cask*, Derek A. Kamal's solitaire innkeeping RPG from Shoreless Skies, illustrated by Claudia Cangini. Not a tavern tycoon game, he stresses — no ledgers, no accounting empire. Paper, pencil, a handful of d6s and a great many charts.

Creation is all rolled. The inn sits beside a large river, stained birch panelling and cushioned booths, and — on a 4 — is a syndicate hideout. Merchants and traders are the clientele, the signature drink a chai bock he names the Spicy Trappist, the signature meal moon-goat shawarma. Quiet live music, themed dinners as its unique service, kegs shuffled constantly to confuse invisible thieves, and a pet ocelot named Monty. Innkeeper Harlan Peters rolls up a half-elf in old adventurer's garb who left an assassin's guild and is, conveniently, a good cook with a hard time slowing down. Staff: Odo the alchemist and Oelia the brewer.

Play is the events table — common guests, brewing and service orders, cooking, trouble, rare guests. Odo botches his first customer and loses morale; Harlan aces a Body 3 check to welcome Lark, a level-two hedge mage, who is packed off to Quadspear Lake to deal with drowned water rats and returns with steel tree bark.

----

Charts as story engine. Does rolling up a world like this spark your imagination, or do you want a firmer authored hand?
